resolution: Made the model painting's durable form the STROKE PROGRAM instead of the rasterized atlas — the load-bearing storage change the user said the paint tools need before real authoring (rasterized pixels corrupt authored data by design; a dither brush is the worst case for RLE and bloats PNG). New framework/gpu/paint_program.zig records every authoring dab/fill as a resolution-independent op (face + barycentric, so it's camera-free and survives detail changes); colour inks are inline and shader inks embed their WGSL + params so the serialized blob is self-contained and replay re-bakes the material with no catalog. Recording is hooked into 3d.zig's authoring entries (paintStampAt/paintAt); replay (paint_program.apply) calls model_paint directly and suppresses recording so it never re-records, with model_paint.clearAtlas giving it a blank canvas and the caller setting the program's detail first (a mesh re-upload) so dabs land at the right resolution. Doors __model_paint_program_read/_apply expose it as base64, and the material door registers its recipe into the program. On the JS side PaintVariant now stores format:'program' (the stroke program) instead of base64 RGBA; save reads the program and load replays it, while legacy atlas variants still load — the atlas is now a pure derived cache. Verified: zig ast-check on all four host files, esbuild transform on both cart files, and all std.ArrayList API usage matches in-tree precedent (mesh_import.zig). Needs the user's framework rebuild to activate; animation as a frame-timings payload rides the same op stream next.
